claims.text: The as-cast Nb-Ta-Ti-V-Zr alloy is chemically disordered and has high lattice disorder and short-range chemical randomness.
Annealing at approximately 1200°C for several hours followed by water quenching increases chemical short-range ordering in Nb-Ta-Ti-V-Zr.
The specified annealing and quenching treatment reduces lattice disorder.
Increased atomic ordering lowers electron-scattering rates.
Increased atomic ordering modifies the electronic band structure.
The ordering-induced electronic-band changes enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling promotes superconducting pairing in this alloy.
Reduced electron scattering and enhanced electron-phonon coupling trigger and enhance low-temperature superconductivity in Nb-Ta-Ti-V-Zr.
Annealed and quenched samples will exhibit a clear superconducting transition.
Annealed and quenched samples will have a higher critical temperature than the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast baseline is expected either not to superconduct within the test range or to have a significantly suppressed critical temperature.
The proposed mechanism applies only when thermal treatment does not change the overall composition or cause phase segregation.
Annealing may cause unintended compositional changes or phase separation that obscure the effect of atomic ordering on superconductivity.
A failure of the treated samples to show a higher critical temperature than the as-cast samples would falsify the ordering-based hypothesis.
